description: Somos un equipo motivado y unido por nuestra pasión por el espacio, la ciencia, la ingeniería y la tecnología. Con diferentes fortalezas y perspectivas, nuestro objetivo es combinar creatividad, trabajo en equipo y resolución de problemas para crear algo significativo para las aplicaciones espaciales de la NASA. Estamos aquí para aprender, desafiarnos a nosotros mismos y convertir ideas ambiciosas en realidad.
summary: Fire in microgravity environments behaves radically differently than on Earth. In enclosed habitats such as the International Space Station or a lunar colonization dome, understanding fire physics and combustion dynamics is critical for crew survival. Therefore, our team developed a web-based dashboard that enables users to gather, catalog, organize, display, and interact with comprehensive datasets derived from NASA fire research and material flammability testing. Engaging with this database is designed to strengthen fire prevention through knowledge while also introducing a dedicated flame-suppression prototype engineered specifically for microgravity environments. Without buoyancy-driven thermal convection, flames assume spherical shapes and disperse toxic gases unpredictably, demanding intuitive analytical tools to assess real-time cabin hazards. Our platform streamlines the visual exploration of each experiment through dynamic filtering and comparative metrics, transforming complex scientific data into accessible insights for researchers, students, and flight crews. Ultimately, this system not only centralizes aerospace fire-safety records, but also fosters the development of autonomous, sustainable suppression solutions capable of safeguarding human life during future space exploration missions.
details:
Fire safety in microgravity is a critical challenge for future space exploration, and complex scientific data often remains inaccessible. To bridge this gap, we built an interactive knowledge hub powered by verified PSI and NASA Physical Sciences Informatics data, enabling users to explore spacecraft fire hazards, materials, experiments, and combustion modeling.

Our platform also introduces VORTEX-0G, a conceptual zero-gravity fire extinguisher engineered to draw in flames and smoke, pass them through a liquid medium for rapid cooling and extinguishment, and filter the air before clean discharge. Alongside this prototype, the hub integrates modules on fire detection, suppression systems, cabin risks, and a built-in AI assistant to guide users through the data. Built with Claude and Stitch, our solution transforms complex NASA research into an intuitive educational tool, accelerating fire prevention awareness for the next generation of space missions.
dataRefs: Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) source of the data upon which the NASA Space App is to be based.
https://psi.nasa.gov/physci/repo/search?q=combustion
NASA Combustion Science: Basic information about most of the combustion investigations for which data is found in the PSI Data Repository.
https://www.nasa.gov/glenn/glenn-expertise-space-exploration/physical-sciences-program/combustion-science/
NASA ScienceCasts: The Power of Studying Combustion on the ISS: Introduction to NASA’s combustion research on the International Space Station through a 3.6-minute video clip from 2018.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W1oXykoz9zg

A Researcher’s Guide to International Space Station Combustion Science: A 2015 review of NASA’s combustion research conducted on, or planned for, the International Space Station. Basic information about most of the combustion investigations described in this 50+ page document is found within the PSI Data Repository.
https://www.nasa.gov/missions/station/a-researchers-guide-to-combustion-science/
Apollo 1: Information about the crew mission, fire that erupted during a pre-launch test killing the crew, investigation, and lessons learned.
https://sma.nasa.gov/sma-disciplines/accllp/apollo-1
Apollo 13: Information about the crew, mission, oxygen tank explosion that occurred during the flight to the Moon, investigation, and lessons learned.
https://sma.nasa.gov/sma-disciplines/accllp/apollo-13

25 Years Ago: Fire Aboard Space Station Mir: Basic information about a fire—caused by an oxygen generator failure—that erupted within the Russian space station Mir in 1997 during joint operations in preparation for the International Space Station (first occupied in 2000).
https://www.nasa.gov/history/25-years-ago-fire-aboard-space-station-mir/
Fireman’s Air Tanks: Basic information about the 1970s adaptation of spacesuit technology to improve firefighters’ air tanks and breathing gear.
https://spinoff.nasa.gov/node/9582

Fire Detector: Basic information about a 1970s smoke detector developed for the shuttle that, discriminating between smoke and dust, results in less nuisance alarms. As such, it has industrial applications (e.g., in mining operations).
https://spinoff.nasa.gov/node/9407
New Technology for the Fire Attire: Basic information about a 1980s application of NASA spacesuit technology to improve firefighter clothing.
https://spinoff.nasa.gov/node/9918
